Hi Jason / Verdant procurement team —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can align pricing/packaging to your purchasing rules before procurement pulls paperwork: 

Call recap (short):
- Verdant liked the Hosted offering for initial rollout; Dedicated came up for predictable latency at scale, and Private (VPC) is a requirement if data residency or certs are mandated.
- Main procurement question: which payment & contracting route do you prefer (PO on Net30, corporate card, or AWS Marketplace)?
- Timeline: you mentioned a typical PO cycle of ~3–4 weeks, but that can vary based on SOW and vendor forms.

Questions / asks for procurement:
1) Preferred billing path: please confirm if PO/Net30 is the default, or if they prefer a marketplace purchase.
2) Finance contact: please share the name/email for anyone who will sign invoices / supplier forms (you mentioned Jason on the call).
3) Commitment preference: are you evaluating committed reserved capacity (12-mo) for a better unit price, or do you need on-demand pricing for pilot flexibility?
4) Any mandatory supplier paperwork or tax/registration steps we should prepare for?

What I recommend next (so procurement can move quickly):
- I attach a short pricing options deck that maps Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with commit vs on-demand cost delta.
- If PO/Net30 is preferred, we can send a draft SOW + standard Redwood vendor packet immediately.
- If you want Marketplace to avoid supplier onboarding, we can provide a marketplace SKU and a short integration checklist.

Next steps: please reply with the preferred billing route and the finance contact. If helpful, we can set a 30-min alignment next week with finance + technical lead.

Thanks — happy to make this as frictionless as possible.

Best,
Olga Petrov

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few answers from procurement:

- Preferred billing path: PO / Net30 is our standard for new vendors. We will consider Marketplace if the licensing and attachments are identical and the account team confirms price parity.
- Finance contact: Jason Miller (jason.miller@verdanthealth.com) — he will need the draft SOW, Redwood vendor form, W-9, and an invoice example.
- Commit vs on-demand: for a pilot (2–3 months) we prefer on-demand (no long commit). For production rollout we evaluate 12-month committed pricing against forecasted spend.

Olga —

Thanks for sending — notes and suggested playbook below after reading Verdant procurement's reply.

Short recommendation (three routes):
1) Marketplace (fastest): If Verdant can buy via AWS Marketplace we can get them into production quickly; typically handled with a card or consolidated AWS billing. Confirm with Jason whether they want marketplace billing linked to their account. Pros: no supplier onboarding, faster PO-to-pay. Cons: marketplace SKUs can have fixed term and sometimes different cancellation rules.

2) Hosted invoiced (PO / Net30): Standard enterprise flow. We provide SOW + vendor pack (W-9, vendor questionnaire), Redwood issues invoices monthly or per-commit. Suitable if they need Net30. Pros: fits their procurement rules. Cons: onboarding 2–4 weeks depending on internal review.

3) Dedicated / Private with commit: If they decide to commit 12 months for Dedicated pool, we can offer committed rates (approx 20–30% unit cost reduction vs on-demand hosted) and a reserved capacity SLA. Requires procurement lead time and legal review for terms. Good for production readiness.

Operational asks for sales engineer to collect before sending SOW:
- Exact billing contact (Jason) and billing address + tax id
- Expected pilot dates and target throughput (to size Dedicated if they ask)
- Any required vendor packet fields (e.g., PO format, third-party security forms)

I’ll draft a short SOW template that defaults to Hosted on-demand and includes an alternate dedicated commit schedule so procurement can see both lanes. Marissa — can you add the 12-mo committed pricing table into the deck?

Karthik
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
